I am an altogether different person this year.
But I still feel like the 13 year old me is watching me over.
I remember how she never wanted to grow up, thinking she will lose the magic of childhood and the ability to just be free.
I know I did, and in many ways, it's true.
We do lose that freedom, that innocence.
But what I also know is that we gain something better.
We gain a different kind of freedom.
The freedom to do what we want, when we want.
The freedom to say no to things that don't feel right, to say yes to things that we want.
We gain the freedom to make mistakes, and to learn from them.
The freedom to fall down, and to get up again.
But we also gain more.
We gain more love, more love from people who actually know us now.
We gain more people who care about us, more friends who will sit with us and talk to us.
We gain a brain that can do more, can think more.
We can think about things that we used to not understand.
We can think about things that will make us happy, and things that will make us sad.
We can think about what we want to do with our life.
I am not the same person that I was when I was 13.
I am different, and that is okay.
You are different too, Sidra.
You are not the same person that you were when you were 13.
But that is okay.
You are a new person now.
A new person with new things to do, and new things to think about.
You are also the same person that you were when you were 13.
You are still the same person with the same heart.
And that is what is most important.

sentences.sentence: Liz’s Bio and Featured Stories
If you like true stories with a twist and a life lesson takeaway, read on!
Photo Courtesy of the Author
Dear Reader,
Welcome to my little corner of the world!

I don’t often lie on the beach, but when I do, I realize how much more than the sand the ocean has to offer... My first thought when I saw him was he was a nice guy, so when I had a chance, I asked for his number...
So I have to admit that there was an unexpected twist when he said that he was coming from a very small town and I had to tell him I had been there, too.
Small world.
He also told me that he liked the beach so that we could go back to the beach.
That sounds like a plan.
Well that was what he said, but the real plan was to go to the lake.
There was no beach.
The place was dry as the dessert.
You can learn a lot from this experience.
Don’t be so quick to make a decision that you need to know if it is right or wrong.
Take your time and find out.
In this story, I was like that.
When I heard where he was from and that he wanted to go back to the beach, that was good enough for me.
But, if I had taken my time, I would have found out where he really wanted to go.
So my advice is, don’t be in such a hurry.
Also, the thing that really makes me sad about this is that I didn’t get the chance to meet him because he said he was going to get out of the truck and that he would be right back.
I was standing in the way.
I was too close.
I didn’t know he wanted to park and then get out of the truck, so I didn’t move.
That was a big mistake.

sentences.sentence: Illustration by Fresh Idea
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of August.
A great chance to market my book.
A great chance to make my book known.
The first draft went quickly, and it was on June 25th when I said to myself, "I think I did it."
But then something happened, and it changed my whole day.
When I got the feedback from my critique group, that's when I started to panic.
They thought that my main character was very mean, and they thought that I was the main character.
That made them not like my book.
I know now that I should not have taken it so hard.
I should have just thanked them for their input and then written a better story.
My ego did.
My ego is like a monster that sits on my shoulder and tells me that everyone is wrong and that my book is perfect just the way it is.
So I didn't write another version of my manuscript, and I just sent it in like it was.
I thought that everyone would like it and that it would be good.
But they didn't, and it wasn't.
Now I know that my ego was wrong, and that I should have listened to my critique group.
I should have taken the time to make my story better.
But my ego didn't want me to, because it liked what I wrote.
It didn't want to change.
I wish that I could go back and talk to that person who wrote the first draft, because I would tell them that they need to write another one.
Writing is hard, but it's not hard because of the words.
Writing is hard because of the person who is writing.

sentences.sentence: How prepared are you for the revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making it big in the business.
You got the location right, you had good food at good prices, and you gave excellent customer service.
It seemed like an easy recipe for success: put it all together and people would come to your restaurant.
The formula was pretty standard:
- Get the location right.
You need a good view, you need to be on the corner, you need to be where the action is.
Location is one of the most important things.
You can't have a restaurant that's in a bad place.
No matter how good the food is, people won't come.
So the location has to be good.
- The food has to be good too.
It's not just enough to have good food.
The food has to be good and you have to have a good price for it.
If your food is too expensive, people won't come and if your food is too bad, they won't come either.
- Finally, you have to have good customer service.
Good customer service is when the server is friendly and gives you what you want.
They bring you food and drinks on time and they make you feel happy.
If the customer isn't happy, they won't come back and they will tell their friends that they shouldn't go to your restaurant.
That formula used to be pretty standard and it worked pretty well.
But things are changing now.
The world is changing fast and the old way of doing things isn't working any more.
More and more people are staying at home and eating and it's not the restaurants fault that people are not eating at the restaurant.
More and more people are eating at home because they can now order food from their phones and get it delivered to them at their houses.

sentences.sentence: **The #1 Thing That Gets Me Through Difficult Days**
My coping mechanism in trying times.
Photo by Ian Chen on Unsplash
I remember the first few hours after my mother took her last breath.
I remember the numbness, the tears, and the emptiness inside.
But what I remember even more is the voice.
It was a recording of her, a message she had left for me many years ago, in case I needed to hear from her again.
She had told me that she loved me and that I would always be okay, and when my dad put that recording on and played it for me, I started to cry.
I wasn't going to be okay right then.
My whole life had changed.
I also remember the first few days.
Those were really hard.
People would tell me that I should be strong for my dad, that I should be brave, that I should try to smile.
But I couldn't be strong.
I couldn't be brave.
And I couldn't smile.
I felt sad, I felt empty, I felt broken.
But even though I was feeling those things, I also felt like I was not alone.
The recording of my mom was with me and that made me feel like I was going to be okay.
The recording of my mom is my everything now.
It gets me through hard days like the first few days after she was gone.
It reminds me what she used to say to me.
It tells me that I will be okay.
And when I am listening to it, I feel like she is still with me and that she will always be with me.
I don't know what I would do if I didn't have that recording.
I would probably just be here, sitting in the dark and crying all the time.
That recording helps me to see that there is more to life than just the now.
There's my mom's voice from the past.

sentences.sentence: **The Dark Side of 'Don't I Know You'**
As the fourth and final song faded, the DJ in our club at the north end of Waikiki kept the crowd pumped for another set of nude women on stage under the flashing black lights.
These men were mostly military dudes who were barely legal, dancing around with open bottles of beer in their hands.

Then I saw her, walking towards me, and I remembered where I had seen her before.
She was my old friend's sister.
I had seen her many times when I was at my friend's house.
I didn't know her name, but I knew her.
And that is when I realized how stupid it is to think that you don't know people.
We all run into each other at some point.
It's funny how we think that we know everyone, or don't know anyone.
But it's probably somewhere in the middle.
I have run into people I knew before when I was at the club, at the beach, at the store, and even on the street.
I'm sure you have too.
The next time you are at a club or a bar, or at the beach, and you don't know anyone, don't worry.
You probably know someone.

sentences.sentence: Simple Changes That Helped Me Lose 5 Kg and Feel Great in Just One Month
Image by biscotto87
When the pandemic-induced lockdown happened, I lost all motivation.
My lifestyle became sedentary.
Up until then, I had been quite active, going to the gym 3 times a week, but once I got stuck at home, I found myself mindlessly watching TV for hours or scrolling through my phone.
I started eating more, eating junk food, pizza, and ice cream almost every day, and I thought I would never be able to get back on track.
But then I realized that I had a goal to set, I had to make a plan and then I could start making changes.
I set a goal to lose 5 kg in a month, it was a small goal, but I wanted to try.
First, I started keeping track of how much I was eating.
I didn't want to eat too much, so I weighed out my meals.
I was eating 3 meals and 2 snacks a day, that was a lot, so I cut that back to 2 meals and 1 snack a day.
And I cut back on how much I was eating at each meal.
For example, if I used to eat a whole pizza, I would now only eat half of it.
I was eating a lot of junk food, so I started to eat healthier, I was eating vegetables with my dinner and I was drinking a lot of water.
I also started exercising more.
I didn't want to go to the gym, so I started going for a walk every day.
I would walk for 30 minutes in the morning and then I would walk for 30 minutes at night.
That was a good start.
The next thing I did was to drink less.
I was drinking a lot of soda, so I started to drink water instead.
And I was drinking a lot of coffee, so I cut that back too.
